- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 0.17 negative values in recent days), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline after peak), model overestimates continuation; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day of divergence.
- When sentiment is positive but price history shows volatility, model tends to over-forecast; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce peak sensitivity.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early downward trend; if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–4% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day high, and sentiment is neutral or negative, apply correction: subtract 2–5% of forecast value for next 3–5 days.
